topic: Computer Networks - Transport Layer: TCP vs UDP
summary: The transport layer provides process-to-process delivery using port numbers. It includes two main protocols: TCP and UDP. TCP is a connection-oriented, reliable protocol that uses a three-way handshake, sequence numbers, acknowledgements, flow control, and congestion control to ensure data arrives correctly and in order. It has a header size of 20 to 60 bytes and is used for HTTP/HTTPS, email, and file transfer. In contrast, UDP is a connectionless, unreliable protocol without handshakes, acknowledgements, or retransmission, making it faster and subject to lower delay. UDP has a fixed header size of 8 bytes and is used for DNS queries, online gaming, live video streaming, and VoIP. As a rule of thumb, choose TCP when every byte must arrive correctly and in order, and choose UDP when low delay matters more than losing a few packets.
